PAPERS.title: Calibration of Low-Cost Particulate Matter Sensors for Exposure Assessment: A Critical Review
PAPERS.pm: Calibrated R2 and RMSE of low-cost PM sensors against reference instruments, laboratory vs field
PAPERS.n: Sixty-six studies, 32 laboratory evaluations and 34 field studies. Median calibrated R2 was 0.92 (n = 31) in the laboratory against 0.72 (n = 29) in the field, and median RMSE 2.6 ug/m3 (n = 7) against 12.3 ug/m3 (n = 9) - a factor of nearly five in error on crossing from bench to deployment. The authors are explicit that these are summaries of a heterogeneous literature, not a pooled effect: aerosol mixture, comparison instrument, concentration range, averaging interval and validation design all differ. RH and temperature were handled in most studies; ML and hybrid models appear more often in field work and sometimes lower error, but independent validation across time, place and sensor unit is uneven. Limitation: only 7 and 9 studies reported RMSE at all, so the headline error figures rest on a small and probably favourable subset. Relevance: high - this is the reference statement that calibration does not transfer, which is the standing assumption behind every distributed network claim in this corpus.

PAPERS.title: Size-Resolved Characteristics and Source Influences of Airborne Microplastics in Central Los Angeles
PAPERS.pm: PM10-associated airborne microplastics (counts/m3, morphology, size) with PM10 composition
PAPERS.n: Two seasonal campaigns in central Los Angeles: microplastics were in every sample at 2.2-4.0 MP/m3 (cool season) and 2.2-3.4 MP/m3 (warm), dominated by fibres and by the 5-50 and 50-100 um size fractions. Total MP correlated strongly (rho >= 0.79) with crustal (Fe, Si, Mn, Ca, Al, Mg), traffic (Ba, Cu, Ni) and carbonaceous (OC, EC) tracers, while short-term meteorology showed no consistent relationship, implying MPs travel as part of the resuspended urban particle mixture rather than as a separate contaminant. Limitation: a preprint; microscopy-based MP counts carry large operator and blank uncertainty, correlation with crustal tracers is also what resuspension artefact looks like, and particles under 5 um - the inhalable fraction - are not resolved. Relevance: moderate-high - supports the same-day tyre-wear argument that the growing non-exhaust, coarse, resuspended fraction is what networks increasingly measure badly.

PAPERS.title: Meteorological modulation of ground-level air quality in India based on in situ measurements
PAPERS.pm: PM10, PM2.5, O3, NO2, SO2 with PBL height, RH, temperature, precipitation, wind, surface pressure (2017-2024)
PAPERS.n: Eight years of in-situ measurements across Indian monitoring sites with Sen's slope trends. PM2.5 fell at several Indo-Gangetic sites (-0.893 to -0.097 ug/m3/month) and PM10 likewise (-1.320 to -0.169), while Punjab rose on local sources; ozone increased (0.041 to 0.529 ug/m3/month), read as aerosol inhibition weakening plus more precursors. Declining boundary-layer height and wind speed over north and east India modulate all of it. Limitation: Sen's slope on eight years of CPCB data cannot separate emission change from meteorological trend, which is the paper's own point turned against its trend estimates; station siting and instrument changes over that period are undocumented. Relevance: moderate - the regional version of the same-day argument that a concentration trend is not an emissions trend.

PAPERS.title: Air Quality and Emission Trends Following the 2021 Environmental Code Reform in Kazakhstan Across Regions and Industrial Sectors
PAPERS.pm: Stationary-source emissions (PM2.5, SO2, CO, NO2) and ambient indicators by region and sector
PAPERS.n: A before-and-after comparison of Kazakhstan's 2021 Environmental Code reform, which tightened standards and pushed Best Available Techniques. Reported stationary-source emissions fell roughly 5-6% between 2021 and 2024, but no statistically significant improvement in assessed ambient indicators appeared between 2021 and 2025, and episodic PM exceedances persisted in several cities. Limitation: no control region and no counterfactual, so the null is as much about the design as about the policy; reported emissions are self-declared inventory, and the ambient network is sparse enough that a 5% emission change would be undetectable even if real. Relevance: moderate - a clean example of why policy evaluation needs measurement density the regulatory network does not have; the 7 October congestion-pricing record is the version that had it.

PAPERS.journal: Chin Med J Pulm Crit Care Med
PAPERS.title: Trends in lung cancer burden, risk factors, and disease projections in China and the United States, 1990-2023
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2023 risk-factor attribution including ambient and household air pollution
PAPERS.n: GBD 2023 data with joinpoint regression, three-factor Das-Gupta decomposition and Bayesian age-period-cohort projection to 2050, comparing lung cancer burden and its attributable risks - smoking, air pollution, occupational exposure, metabolic and dietary factors - between China and the United States. Limitation: GBD attribution for air pollution is a modelled counterfactual built on exposure surfaces and borrowed concentration-response functions, so the pollution share is an assumption propagated forward, not an observation; the abstract reports no attributable fractions. Relevance: low-moderate - useful as the burden framing that the measurement side of this corpus feeds, but it adds no exposure information of its own.

PAPERS.title: Regime-Dependent Effectiveness of Spectral Nudging in WRF-Chem: Meteorological and Saharan Dust Skill over the Central Mediterranean
PAPERS.pm: Modelled Saharan dust AOD550 against AERONET; meteorological RMSE from nudged vs free runs
PAPERS.n: A two-tier design separates the meteorological response to spectral nudging (a 104-day chemistry-free pair) from the dust-transport response (paired event simulations). Nudging improves sea-level pressure most (daily RMSE 2.08 to 1.53 hPa) and 10 m wind less (2.50 to 2.20 m/s), while 2 m temperature does not improve (2.05 to 2.15 C); the benefit recurs episodically rather than growing with simulation age. Dust skill is conditional: in the weakly forced June case all seven AERONET sites improved (station-mean RMSE 0.457 to 0.235, correlation 0.778 to 0.881), while in March RMSE fell at all eight sites but mean correlation was unchanged. Limitation: two outbreaks is a thin basis for a regime claim, and AOD is a column integral that constrains surface dust PM only weakly. Relevance: moderate - dust is the event class where satellite-and-model PM products diverge most from surface nodes.

PAPERS.title: Interaction of maternal PM2.5 exposure and psychosocial state on newborn macrosomia: A nationwide population-based study
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - maternal PM2.5 exposure with psychosocial state, nationwide (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: the publisher deposited title, authors and DOI on 10 Oct with no abstract, and the retry chain recovered none. By title, a nationwide study of the interaction between maternal PM2.5 exposure and maternal psychosocial state on newborn macrosomia. Interaction claims between a modelled environmental exposure and a self-reported psychosocial measure are the design most prone to residual confounding by socioeconomic position, and macrosomia is a thresholded birthweight outcome whose prevalence is sensitive to that. Relevance: moderate - birth cohorts are where personal rather than residential exposure measurement would change the estimate most. On the abstract-retry list.

PAPERS.title: Cleaning the air or shifting the burden? Characterizing urban-rural disparities in air pollution-attributable mortality across Italy
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - urban-rural disparity in PM-attributable mortality across Italy (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: Elsevier deposited title, authors and DOI on 10 Oct with no abstract. By title, an attributable-mortality analysis asking whether Italian air-quality gains have been distributed or merely displaced from urban to rural populations. Rural exposure is systematically the worse-measured half of any national network, so a rural-urban disparity estimate inherits the monitoring asymmetry it is trying to describe - the 8 October US block-level record showed spatial aggregation attenuating exactly this kind of disparity. Relevance: moderate-high; on the abstract-retry list.

PAPERS.title: PM2.5 Composition and Organic Matter Sources in Pretoria, South Africa Employing Fourier Transform-Infrared Spectroscopy
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - FT-IR functional-group speciation of PM2.5 organic matter (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: title, authors and DOI deposited 10 Oct with no abstract. By title, FT-IR functional-group analysis of PM2.5 organic matter in Pretoria with source attribution. FT-IR on routine filters is one of the few speciation routes cheap enough to run network-wide, and sub-Saharan African composition data are scarce enough that any new site matters. Relevance: high for the composition gap this corpus repeatedly hits; on the abstract-retry list.
